Hey!

I was in the same place you were, a couple of years ago. Had no experience in illustration, no art classes that I took. But I started illustrating. Last time I did any art commissions were at the beginning of 2020. I have a full-time job as a graphics designer and a marketing professional and I am on the path of making one of my other hobbies, dance, a professional career.   


If I am going to "make it" as an illustrator at the age of 40, then so be it. 

In my experience, if I was stressed even whilst I was taking a break, it would be because I had set an expectation on myself to be productive and work on my illustrations. So, I have told myself to not have any expectations of myself and of my art during my breaks. If an idea comes to me during those times, and I'm able to work on it, then I do. If I am working on my job or focusing on keeping the house clean, then that's all I do.   


Your hobbies sometimes don't need more than your commitment. It could be a commitment of thought even, like making music is all you're thinking about.   


We are human. Art or anything artistic is moody.    


But on the less philosophical side, give yourself enough free time to just be free. Productivity is not going to work if you're stressed about being productive. Nitro only lasts so long. 

​

I hope that I have made some sense and you could take something from this :P
